subject: Goldshore: workflow export + timeline ask
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@goldshore.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Goldshore RFP - request for per-customer workflow export and SLA

Markus / team — forwarding Goldshore's RFP excerpt and their procurement ask. High level: they want a per-customer workflow/audit export (near-real-time), an ingest-friendly webhook or SFTP delivery, and an explicit availability SLA for the export endpoint (they requested 99.9%). Procurement flagged this as a gating item for the pilot to move to PA (paid acceptance).

Key asks from the prospect (see attached RFP):
- Durable export (per-tenant) of routing/workflow history, tokens and redaction metadata, delivered to their SFTP or via webhook.
- 30-day near-real-time window (streaming or sub-5min batch acceptable).
- Contract requirement: export availability SLA and an incident escalation path.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: delivery of sample export + signed export SLA.

They're on a tight commercial schedule — they need vendor compliance evidence by EOW June 8 to close in Q3.

Questions for product/eng: is there a feasible short-term shim (lambda / export job) we can offer as a contractual commitment while we schedule a product-grade feature? If so, what's realistic timeline and resource estimate?

Attaching: Goldshore_RFP_June2028.pdf, Goldshore_Requirements_Summary.xlsx

Thanks — cc'ing Jasmine for PM and David for eng intake.

—Sean
Sales Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Goldshore_RFP_June2028.pdf]
[Attachment: Goldshore_Requirements_Summary.xlsx]

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Goldshore RFP - request for per-customer workflow export and SLA

Thanks Sean — overview appreciated.

Jasmine / David: this is a clear enterprise gating ask from procurement. Goldshore is a top-tier financial prospect (see deal id). We need a concrete proposal: a) a near-term contractual workaround we can commit to in the deal (non-productized) and b) a product roadmap estimate for a hardened, supported export feature with SLA.

Priorities I see:
- Customer-facing acceptance criteria (what we will deliver for pilot).
- Implementation approach (one-off ETL/export vs. baseline product work).
- Risk and monitoring (how we guarantee the export and what the runbook looks like).
- Economics / eng effort estimate (so I can defend resource tradeoffs).

Can you provide a 1-page option comparison by Monday (June 4)? If we can provide a short-term export path (<= 4 weeks) to satisfy procurement, we can keep the commercial momentum for Q3.

Also: Monica, please confirm whether the customer will accept a time-bound operational commitment ("we will run a dedicated export job for 3 months while product dev proceeds") or if they insist on product-level SLA from day one.

Markus
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Goldshore RFP - request for per-customer workflow export and SLA

Folks — quick customer context from CS:
- Goldshore is running an internal pilot (50 agents) with high volume during market hours. If we can provide per-tenant exports (redacted tokens + routing metadata) they will proceed to a 6-month paid pilot and then scale to production.
- Procurement has strict audit and retention policies. They will not accept a vague "we plan to build" statement — they need something they can include in the SOW.
- The customer team is amenable to a temporary operational solution (scheduled SFTP drops + monitoring) provided we commit to a go-live date within 30 days and a migration plan to productized export within 8–12 weeks.
- They asked for sample export schema and a signed runbook for incidents.

I'll synthesize acceptance criteria and sample schema tonight and upload to the drive link.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Goldshore RFP - request for per-customer workflow export and SLA

Thanks for the context — I reviewed the RFP and the attached requirements. Proposed options (short summary):

Option A — Operational shim (fastest):
- Implement a scheduled export job that pulls per-tenant workflow/audit data, runs redaction, and pushes a CSV/NDJSON to Goldshore SFTP or a signed webhook.
- Timeline: 2–3 weeks (dev + security review + runbook).
- Cost: 2 engineer-weeks + 1 security engineer for review; maintenance is operational.
- SLA: we can commit to an operational availability SLA for the export job (99.5%) with a 24-hour incident response and defined escalation for P1.
- Risk: not productized; scaling and monitoring overhead.

Option B — Product path (recommended long-term):
- Build an export endpoint (tenant-scoped) with streaming/batch delivery, built-in retries, observability, and RBAC.
- Timeline: 8–12 weeks (core work + QA + doc + rollout).
- Cost: feature drop across 2 sprints (3 engineers), with follow-up hardening.
- SLA: can be included in enterprise contracts once productized and load-tested.

Ask to leadership: if dealing team wants Option A for the contract, we need explicit sign-off on expected operational costs and a migration plan to Option B within the agreed window. If leadership prefers to prioritize the product path now, we need to allocate feature sprint capacity (3 engineers) for the next two sprints.

Deliverables I can prepare by EOD Monday: short one-pager with acceptance criteria, sample payload schema, test plan, and a recommended migration timeline.

—Jasmine
PM, Enterprise Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Park <emily.park@goldshore.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Goldshore RFP - request for per-customer workflow export and SLA

Thanks everyone — appreciate the clear options. Goldshore will accept Option A as a contractual commitment for the pilot provided the following are included in the SOW:
- Delivery: nightly exports (or webhook) with max ~5 minute latency for streaming events where feasible.
- Availability: export job availability SLA of 99.5% for the pilot period (we understand product SLA can be higher; procurement will accept 99.5% tied to the operational shim).
- Migration: committed migration plan to a product-grade export within 10 weeks of pilot start.
- Acceptance: delivery of a sample export with schema and a signed runbook before pilot start.

We agree to a short call tomorrow to finalize language — please send a calendar invite. Once SOW language is agreed we can move procurement to signatures.

Emily Park
Director, Platform Integrations
Goldshore Financial
